page: Amazon Web Services r6a.large is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with a dedicated AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz. The configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or a GPU, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25%, while the multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with read-only large block bandwidth at 31.33 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 21.46 GB/sec. Geekbench scores reflect average single-core capabilities but poor multi-core and image processing performance. Database operations and Redis SET operations also register in the bottom 10% of benchmarks.

The r6a.large offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require a larger memory footprint relative to compute power without needing high-performance multi-threaded execution. However, the tradeoffs include limited multi-core scaling, lower memory bandwidth, and the absence of local NVMe storage. This instance is appropriate for memory-intensive workloads with low parallel processing demands, such as small-scale caching, basic text processing, and lightweight database operations that fit entirely within memory.
